bearings.paper_claim: Meat is the outer product of estimating functions with optional n/(n-k) adjustment (Eq. 10, p.6); sandwich errors lose power under correct specification and are useful only if estimates stay consistent; probit age p moves from .033 to .051 (n = 601, Sec 5.2).
bearings.system_side: OLS with sector baselines reports HC1 = (n/df) A X'uu'X A as a reference-only error (sgs_estimate.R lines 35-36); CR1 at sgs_estimate.R lines 44-45; primary inference is a wild cluster restricted bootstrap-t with a t_cr1 statistic (header lines 1-12, sgs_estimate.R line 264).
bearings.transfer_conditions: HC1 and CR1 formulas match Eq. 10 with cluster sums added. The paper's meat assumes independent rows, so within-sector dependence needs CR1, which the paper does not treat. Statsmodels cross-check is in code/tests/test_estimate.py lines 44-45, not tests/ at repo root.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers reproduced at Sec 5.2 (p = 0.03282 to 0.05077). Code lines 35-36 and 44 verified. Softened for the test path (code/tests/test_estimate.py) and for the bootstrap wording, which is a wild cluster restricted bootstrap-t, not a plain bootstrap.

bearings.paper_claim: HAC meat is a weighted sum of lagged estimating-function cross-products (Eq. 11, p.7) behind NeweyWest-type wrappers; no coverage study is reported, and Kiefer-Vogelsang fixed-b testing is named as an alternative (Sec 6, p.14).
bearings.system_side: SEATS-W computes Bartlett Newey-West HAC by hand at lags 2, 4 and 8 weeks within cycle with weights 1 - l/(L+1) and n/(n-p) (sgs_seats.R line 277 and lines 389-400); reported as secondary with no p-value. Primary inference is a residual moving-block bootstrap with fixed regressors, plus a recursive block bootstrap for dynamic models.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Lags, Bartlett weights and n/(n-p) factor match the paper's Eq. 11 setup. The paper gives no finite-sample guarantee, so the caveat that HAC is secondary applies. The 17-week figure appears in the code comment at sgs_seats.R lines 71-77 as an example of an interval, not as a stated cycle length. No second-path check against sandwich::NeweyWest was found in code/tests.
bearings.verifier_note: Lags, weights, secondary-only status and the Holm example verified (sgs_seats.R lines 71-76, 277, 391-400). Softened: primary inference is a fixed-X residual moving-block bootstrap plus a recursive block bootstrap for dynamic models, and 17 weeks is an illustrative example, not a stated cycle length. The missing second-path check is confirmed.

related.why: Real item. The 2006 text cites Zeileis 2004 JSS 11(10) as the linear-model predecessor, and the 2004 text covers HC4 and Andrews-type HAC weights, matching the claim that this paper only cites those details.
Real item. Its title is an object-oriented implementation of clustered covariances in R, which is the CR extension of the same bread and meat framework that the growth study uses via CR1.

summary_issues: Summary says the paper's HC meat ignores cluster dependence and the study handles it with CR1. The meat assumes independent rows, which is verified, but the paper never discusses clustering, so this is the reviewer's inference, not a paper claim.
Summary's gap about the missing HAC second-path check is verified: no NeweyWest or HAC check exists in code/tests. The HAC figures stay UNVERIFIED under DE-062.

Summary's numbers are all verified: Poisson z -2.12 (p .034) to -1.35 (p .18); probit age .033 to .051; n = 250 and n = 601; statsmodels cross-check of HC1 and CR1. The path tests/test_estimate.py should read code/tests/test_estimate.py.
Extraction scope says R 2.x-era package. The paper's simulation calls RNGversion 3.5.0 (Sec 5.1, p.9), so the text is an R 3.5-era reprint. Correct the scope line.

Extraction limitations say the n/(n-k) adjustment has no theoretical support for non-linear models (p.6). The paper says only that the adjustment lacks theoretical justification, with no linear or non-linear qualifier. Soften.

Extraction key finding says the paper claims the same qualitative interpretations for tobit and probit. The paper says results are qualitatively identical for tobit but the picture is only similar for probit, and the probit age term does cross 0.05 (0.0328 to 0.0508). Restrict the claim to tobit.

Extraction citation of the 2006 paper as year 2006 with JSS 16(9) and DOI 10.18637/jss.v016.i09 is verified against the paper's own self-citation (text line 885). Coverage: all numeric claims in ext and rel were checked against the text; theory sections 2-3 were spot-checked only.
